records.name: Florida
records.current_summary: § 553.865 (2023) makes refusing to leave a facility not matching sex assigned at birth — after being told by a government employee — criminal trespass in state-owned buildings. Produced what is believed to be the first arrest under a state trans bathroom law (March 2025, Capitol, held ~24h; charges later dismissed on a technicality — a mixed-leaning-positive institutional response). The state stopped issuing corrected-marker licences and treats “misrepresentation” as potential fraud; Equality Florida and HRC issued named travel advisories. Physical safety is comparatively better than the law suggests: 3.7 killings per 100k trans women/yr, below the worst-law average. Below the national score 0.36.

sources.claim: ACLU of Florida 'Know Your Rights' page (updated March 2024) explaining Fla. Stat. 553.865 (2023): refusing to leave a restroom or changing facility not matching sex assigned at birth, after being told to by a government employee, is criminal trespass in state-owned buildings; the page calls the law 'complex, confusing, and vague' and lays out its limited actual coverage (multi-user facilities in government buildings).

NBC News/AP report (April 2025): Marcy Rheintgen, 20, was arrested on 19 March 2025 after using a women's restroom in the Florida Capitol — believed by civil-rights attorneys to be the first arrest anywhere under a state transgender bathroom criminal ban; a second-degree misdemeanour trespass charge carrying up to 60 days. The article notes that of at least 14 states with bathroom restrictions, only Florida and Utah criminalise the act itself.

Metro Weekly (July 2025): a Leon County judge dismissed the trespass charges against Rheintgen on 20 June 2025 on speedy-trial grounds after the state failed to file charging documents within 90 days; because she was charged with trespass rather than under the 'Safety in Private Spaces Act', she could not challenge the bathroom ban's constitutionality in the case.

Equality Florida press release (11 April 2023): a state-level travel advisory warning of risks to the health, safety and freedom of people travelling to or relocating to Florida, issued in response to laws the organisation calls hostile to the LGBTQ community; the nation's largest LGBTQ advocacy group joined with an updated advisory in 2024. One of only named sub-national travel advisories of its kind in the country.

The Needle (July 2026) state-by-state analysis overlaying legislative-risk maps on recorded trans-homicide data: legal risk predicts how the state treats you, not how people do; this state's recorded killing rate for trans women is 3.7 per 100k/yr, below the worst-law-state average — and all counts are floors from an acknowledged undercount.

flags: 'stopped issuing corrected birth certificates' — audited sources evidence the DRIVER-LICENSE policy (SW) + a general birth-certificate-restriction concern list only; verify FL birth-cert specifics in rework
